Engineering translates the agreed slice into components, dependencies, decisions, risks, verification steps, and an implementation sequence.

Engineering captures build, test, review, and diff evidence. Product finalizes the launch plan and prepares to evaluate the increment.

Iterate against acceptance criteria until evidence supports a decision
Review the increment against agreed criteria, convert feedback into bounded technical changes, and repeat until every criterion has a clear evidence-based decision.
Product compares the increment to intent and gives criterion-specific feedback. The team records each criterion as met, not met, or needing evidence.
FACILITATOR: Require specific feedback tied to the agreed acceptance criteria.
Engineering maps feedback to bounded changes, implements the next revision, reruns checks, and captures test, review, diff, or visual evidence.
FACILITATOR: Prevent scope expansion and preserve traceability from feedback to change.
The team displays the increment again, verifies each criterion, and decides whether to accept, repeat the loop, or explicitly accept a known limitation.
FACILITATOR: Let evidence—not activity—determine whether the team advances.
EXPECTED OUTCOME  •  Criterion-level decisions  •  Traceable feedback and implemented changes  •  Demonstrable increment with evidence  •  Known limitations documented

We build together alongside our clients’ teams, bringing both onshore and near-shore talent and slowly stepping back over time as we enable our clients to move forward with the modernized software​

We meet our clients wherever they’re at. We often take a lead role in standing up the modern architecture and technology stack aligned to best practices, leaning on our onshore resources for deeper engagement with client team members​

Once the foundation and structure is in place, we begin to step back into a supporting role as our clients’ teams take the lead, often augmenting with near-shore resources to scale up and build faster at an attractive price point while coaching and mentoring client team members on the modern platform​
As the client team gains a level of comfort and assurance in maintaining the effort, we fade into the background, often moving on to new problems to solve within the organization​
We fill client team gaps and take a leadership role in establishing processes, architecture, and technologies, getting the modernization effort off to solid start​

As we continue to partner with clients on the modernization roadmap, measuring progress and reprioritizing at each planning horizon, we continually evaluate the balance of WM assistance required to successfully provide value
As our clients’ teams grow confident in handling modernization efforts, we plan the roll off strategy based on client goals as they take on long-term sustainment of the modernized software

West Monroe recommends taking a user-journey focused approach to the modernization program. But identifying and prioritizing user journeys, we can align the modernization and testing strategy approach to ensure that changes are desirable, performant and validated.

CURRENT STATE

POWERBUILDER RETIREMENT
PowerBuilder has become a niche, legacy application stack. West Monroe recommends modernizing to a web-based user interface layer to ensure Pattern can continue to hire skilled engineers, to support a potential SaaS-ification of the product, and alignment with potential desktop and mobile deployment capabilities.

THREE-TIER RESPONSIBILITY
Modern application architecture practices over the last 15 years recommend a 3-tier structure: data access, service/domain, and user interface to ensure each layer can be maintained and upgraded separately. West Monroe recommends aligning to this high-level approach as an outcome of the modernization.

WEB EXPERIENCE ON PREMISES
React provides browser or PWA delivery within the practice network. Embedded and desktop routes remain transition choices. WAN network support could potentially allow multi-site expansion for practices with that network capability.

JOURNEY-LED DELIVERY
By using a journey-led approach, the disruption inside individual critical user journeys is minimized. Piloting specific personas or roles holistically can create a more seamless transition experience for customers. In addition, end to end testing for specific flows can be aligned with the testing workstream.
